items.title: Flick: "Una victoria de 'diez'"
items.description: Hansi Flick se mostró muy contento después de un triunfo muy valioso y calificó el triunfo como un triunfo “de diez”. Con esta puntuación calificó el 1-2 en el Metropolitano, haciendo distinción entre la primera segunda y la segunda, pero dejando claro que “hay que creer en este equipo”.

items.title: Maestro Pedri
items.description: El Barça dio un sensacional golpe a la Liga en la segunda parte del Metropolitano, ganando un partido muy difícil a un buen Atlético que dominó la primera mitad. Dos jugadores brillaron en el FC Barcelona: Fermín, que consiguió los dos goles y Lamine, que fue un prodigio en la ofensiva blaugrana, desbordando, creando peligro, dando asistencias. Pero el maestro del triunfo fue Pedri, el jugador que, sin Rodri en el equipo, lideró el control de la pelota en la segunda mitad, con la entrada de De Jong también, primero en el lateral derecho. Un tropiezo antes del parón hubiera supuesto un golpe negativo y el Barça le dio la vuelta a todo y mantuvo el liderato y la confianza en su juego.

items.title: Barcelona move clear at the top after Fermín López’s double stuns Atlético Madrid
items.description: They had been in a battle, they had been behind and they had been on edge, but Barcelona found a way through, holding on to their place at the top of the table and holding the doubts at bay for another day. A fortnight in which they were defeated by Paris Saint-Germain and Real Madrid, in which they might have wondered if something was not right, ended with a 2-1 win at Atlético Madrid. This was a proper test and a proper game, 10 World Cup winners on the field and first place awaiting the winner, and at the end of an intense enjoyable night, that was Hansi Flick’s side.At a noisy Metropolitano, the atmosphere matching the occasion, against a frenetic Atlético side that went for the throat, Barcelona trailed to a Giuliano Simeone goal and for a while in a frenzied first half it looked like there may be no way back. But they found it, two goals from Fermín López either side of the break leading them to the kind of victory that brings a reward beyond the points. It hadn’t been easy but they had made it; ultimately, they might conclude they had found a way to manage it too, some satisfaction in the suffering, in how they resisted and re-established control amid the chaos. items.title: Fermín Lopez saves Barcelona with stunning brace in dramatic Atletico Madrid comeback
items.description:
Barcelona produced a stunning comeback to defeat Atletico Madrid and restore their three-point lead at the top of La Liga. 
Barcelona produced a stunning comeback to defeat Atletico Madrid and restore their three-point lead at the top of La Liga. Diego Simeone’s side made the stronger start and took the lead through Simeone in the 10th minute, but Fermín Lopez equalised just before half-time, shifting the momentum in Barcelona’s favour.



Barcelona grew in confidence after the break, with Lopez completing his brace after receiving a through ball from Lamine Yamal and producing an excellent finish. Atletico had opportunities to find another equaliser but failed to convert, while López was officially named Man of the Match after contributing two goals to the comeback.



The midfielder continues to enjoy an outstanding season, having registered 15 goal contributions (eight goals and seven assists). His latest performance proved decisive in a result that strengthens the Blaugrana’s position at the summit of the La Liga standings.

items.title: Cristiano Ronaldo is the odd one out as Lionel Messi and Neymar share curious detail from their final international games
items.description:
heir departures came in very different circumstances, but a curious connection between their final international appearances has added another layer to the end of an era. 
Cristiano Ronaldo joined Lionel Messi and Neymar in bringing his international career to an end in 2026, marking an extraordinary year for soccer after three of the sport’s biggest names stepped away from their national teams. Their departures came in very different circumstances, but a curious connection between their final international appearances has added another layer to the end of an era.



Neymar‘s farewell followed Brazil’s elimination from the 2026 World Cup, while Messi received an emotional send-off in front of Argentina supporters. Ronaldo’s departure from Portugal was more complicated, with tensions surrounding his relationship with coach Jorge Jesus and the Portuguese Football Federation (FPF) attracting attention.



Santos’ captain was the first of the trio to bring his international career to a close. The Brazilian had indicated that the 2026 World Cup would be his final tournament with the Selecao, and he made his last appearance in the round of 16 against Norway.



Despite Brazil suffering a 2-1 defeat, Neymar found the net, scoring a late goal that ended the national team’s remarkable 79-match scoring streak. The result meant his final international appearance came in a painful elimination, although he still managed to leave the tournament with one last goal for his country.



🚨 End of an era. Neymar has announced his retirement from international football with Brazil.“I tried. I tried. It started here at MetLife Stadium and I finished here. It is now over.”From his 2010 debut at the same stadium to tonight’s heartbreaking 2-1 R16 exit vs Norway… pic.twitter.com/kmUHNYuHiG— Dr RK Singh (@DrRupak) July 6, 2026



Messi‘s farewell unfolded in much happier circumstances. Following Argentina’s World Cup final defeat, the legendary captain decided to end his international career, with the national team arranging a memorable send-off against Benin at the Monumental. Argentina won 3-0, with the 39-year-old superstar scoring once and providing two assists in front of an emotional home crowd.









Ronaldo’s Portugal farewell takes different turn



Ronaldo’s international retirement came later in the year, officially ending his extraordinary career with Portugal on November 5, 2026. His departure followed a turbulent period involving his exit from the national team’s October camp and subsequent reconciliation with Jorge Jesus.



The announcement arrived shortly before Jorge Jesus’ November squad selection, adding to speculation about the relationship between the captain, the coach and the federation. Unlike Messi, Ronaldo has so far shown little interest in arranging a dedicated farewell match.



Cristiano Ronaldo #7 of Portugal applauds fans



His final international goal had come earlier in the 2026 World Cup, when he helped Portugal secure a 2-1 comeback victory over Croatia in the round of 32. However, his final appearance for the national team would ultimately prove different from those of his two fellow superstars.



The curious stat separating Ronaldo from Messi and Neymar



There is a striking distinction between the three legends when looking at the matches that marked the end of their international careers. Ronaldo was the only member of the trio who failed to score in his final appearance for his national team.



Cristiano Ronaldo #7 of Portugal shows dejection



Neymar scored against Norway despite Brazil’s elimination, while Messi found the net during Argentina‘s 3-0 victory over Benin. Ronaldo, meanwhile, finished his Portugal career without adding another goal to his international record after his final strike against Croatia.



Los tres se retiraron de sus selecciones el mismo año. Su último gol fue de penalti y los tres lo patearon hacia el mismo lado.Cosas del destino y sus caprichos. pic.twitter.com/9a2usO4GpW— ALXN ❄️ (@alansitoo_20) November 6, 2026 



Yet another remarkable coincidence connects the three players: each scored his final international goal from the penalty spot. The accompanying video highlights the similarities between their last successful penalties, with Neymar and Messi reportedly sending their efforts towards the same side while Ronaldo opted for the center.

items.title: Atletico Madrid vs Barcelona: Confirmed lineups for the 2026-27 LaLiga match
items.description:
Take a look at the projected lineups for Atletico Madrid vs Barcelona in the 2026-27 LaLiga. Atletico Madrid host Barcelona in a LaLiga clash that carries real weight near the top of the table, with Diego Simeone’s side looking to keep pace and Hansi Flick’s group chasing another statement win.
Atletico Madrid come into this one on a run of three straight wins, beating Levante 2-0 on October 31, Deportivo 1-0 on October 24 and Espanyol 1-0 on October 17. None of those results have come with much margin, but the clean sheets in all three show a side built on a solid defensive base under Simeone. A fourth straight win would send a strong signal that Atletico Madrid belong in the title picture.
Barcelona arrive off a 6-1 rout of Alaves last Saturday, a result that followed a 1-2 loss to Real Madrid on October 25 and a 5-2 win over Betis back on October 17. The scoreline against Alaves points to an attack firing on all cylinders, even if the defeat to their fiercest rival is still fresh. A win at the Metropolitano would answer any lingering questions after that loss and keep Barcelona firmly in the title race.
Atletico Madrid confirmed lineup
Simeone sets Atletico Madrid up in a 4-2-3-1, with Jan Oblak behind a back line of Marcos Llorente, Dávid Hancko, Marc Pubill and Álex Grimaldo. Koke and Pablo Barrios sit as the double pivot, giving the team cover to let Lee Kang-in, Giuliano Simeone and Álex Baena work around Julián Alvarez up top. Johnny is out, but the rest of the group is otherwise at full strength and set up to stay compact before looking to spring forward through Alvarez and Baena.
Atletico Madrid confirmed starting XI (4-4-2): Jan Oblak, Marcos Llorente, Alejandro Grimaldo, Koke, Marc Pubill, Dávid Hancko, Giuliano Simeone, Pablo Barrios, Julián Alvarez, Lee Kang-In, Álex Baena. Coach: Diego Simeone.
Barcelona confirmed lineup
Flick also goes with a 4-2-3-1 for Barcelona, built around Joan García in goal and a back four of Brian Fariñas Pérez, Pau Cubarsí, Gerard Martín and João Cancelo. Marc Bernal and Pedri anchor midfield, feeding Fermín López, Lamine Yamal and Anthony Gordon behind Raphinha. The absences of Dani Olmo, Xavi Espart, Roony Bardghji and Juan Hernández thin out Flick’s attacking options from the bench, putting extra weight on the front four to create and finish chances against a well organized Atletico Madrid defense.
Barcelona confirmed starting XI (4-3-3): Joan García, Brian Fariñas, João Cancelo, Marc Bernal, Pau Cubarsí, Gerard Martín, Pedri, Fermín López, Raphinha, Lamine Yamal, Anthony Gordon. Coach: Hansi Flick.

items.title: San José se deshace en elogios hacia la Real tras vivir un día especial: "Es mi casa, me formó como jugador y como entrenador"
items.description: El Rayo Vallecano peleó para intentar empatar y eso lo valoró su entrenador Beñat San José. "Estamos muy fastidiados, con mucho dolor, porque creo que lo que se ha visto en el campo no merecía para nada una derrota. En la primera parte ha sido un partido de tú a tú. Sabíamos que la Real, con mucha energía, se iba a arriesgar a apretarnos arriba. Creo que tampoco nos han hecho mucho daño y nosotros hemos tenido varios ataques muy buenos. Hemos tenido ocasiones muy claras, intervenciones extraordinarias del portero de la Real y un balón al poste. Cuando mejor estábamos nos ha llegado el fatídico gol. Nos duele muchísimo irnos así de vacío a casa. No merecíamos perder, la verdad. Creo que merecíamos mínimamente el empate. Estoy contento con el trabajo y el partido que han hecho los jugadores", explicó el donostiarra.

items.title: Zamora Decide exige la remodelación integral de la travesía de Tagarabuena
items.description: Convocados por Zamora Decide, cientos de vecinos de Tagarabuena y Toro, se concentraron durante la mañana del domingo 8 de noviembre en la plaza de la localidad para exigir la remodelación integral de la travesía del barrio. La movilización responde a los problemas que, según denuncian los residentes, han surgido en sus viviendas y bodegas subterráneas tras la ejecución de las obras, especialmente por la aparición de grietas, humedades, filtraciones de agua, malos olores y ruidos, unas incidencias que, aseguran, no se producían antes de la intervención. Actualmente, alrededor de una treintena de viviendas se encuentran afectadas de manera directa, aunque advierten de que «con el tiempo vamos a ser muchas más si esto no se soluciona pronto».

items.title: Matarazzo: "Es muy importante ganar partidos así, cuando no puedes atacar tanto tienes que defender"
items.description: Pellegrino Matarazzo estaba feliz por la victoria del equipo en un día de trabajo, de saber sufrir y de acertar en las ocasiones. "No ha sido fácil hoy pese a empezar bien el partido. Fue una buena primera parte, con ocasiones, centros. No hemos conseguido el 1-0 y la segunda parte ha estado muy abierta, ellos han tenido las claras porque no les hemos seguido en el área. Hemos marcado un fantástico gol, un pase de talla mundial de Barrene y gol de Orri. Sufrir es parte del fútbol. Un equipo como el Rayo, que trabaja duro, que tiene energía y presiona fuerte, no es fácil. Siempre no puede serlo. Toca sufrir a veces para ganar y lo hicimos. Es muy importante ganar partidos así, cuando no te funcionan las cosas ofensivamente", dijo el técnico estadounidense.

items.title: FC Barcelone
items.description: Le FC Barcelone, ou Barça, est un club de football espagnol fondé en 1899, situé en Catalogne. L'équipe, surnommée Blaugrana, évolue au Camp Nou, stade de près de 100.000 places. A son palmarès, 26 titres de champion d'Espagne, 31 Coupes du roi, cinq Ligues des champions notamment. Xavi est l'entraîneur du Barça depuis 2021. Parmi les joueurs phares de l'histoire du club: Lionel Messi, Andres Iniesta, Ronaldinho ou encore Johan Cruyff.

items.title: Atlético de Madrid
items.description: L'Atlético de Madrid est un club espagnol fondé en 1903, qui évolue en Liga. Ses couleurs sont le rouge et le blanc. Ses joueurs sont surnommés les Colchoneros. Le Français Antoine Griezmann est devenu le meilleur buteur de l'histoire de l'Atlético devant Luis Aragones, son joueur le plus capé est Koke. Le club a été sacré 11 fois champion d'Espagne, a été finaliste de la Ligue des champions à trois reprises (1974, 2014, 2016). Son entraîneur emblématique et actuel est Diego Simeone.

items.title: 1-0: La Real se hace fuerte también cuando no brilla y gana sin encajar al Rayo
items.description: Victoria importantísima de la Real Sociedad ante el Rayo en Anoeta, por la mínima y sufriendo, sin brillantez, pero sumando tres puntos clave para dejar atrás los últimos dos pinchazos y afianzar la quinta plaza con 22 puntos, cuatro de ventaja con el sexto, al llegar al segundo parón de la temporada. Y sin encajar goles, que suena mejor, gracias a un gran partido de Remiro. El gol de Óskarsson, por quinta vez en los últimos seis partidos, sirvió a los de Matarazzo para una victoria de trabajo y de valor, sin un Oyarzabal enfermo, Sarr lesionado, y a sumar un Barrenetxea roto justo después de generar el gol del triunfo con su magia. Si esta Real también puede ganar 1-0, pinta bien la cosa. A descansar, lo que se pueda, en el parón.

items.title: Manchester United vs Aston Villa: Confirmed lineups for the 2026-27 Premier League match
items.description:
Take a look at the projected lineups for Manchester United vs Aston Villa in the 2026-27 Premier League. Manchester United host Aston Villa with both sides looking to settle unsettled form, and this one carries weight well beyond the typical early-November fixture.
Manchester United come into this one off three straight defeats in all competitions, having lost 0-2 to Chelsea on October 31 and 0-3 to Bournemouth on October 25, with a 1-1 draw against Leeds on October 18 sandwiched between. That run leaves them without a win in their last three and searching for answers under Michael Carrick. A home game against Villa now looks like a chance to stop the slide rather than extend it.
Aston Villa arrive in much better shape, unbeaten in their last three matches. Unai Emery’s side beat Newcastle 1-0 on October 17 and followed that by beating Manchester City 2-1 on October 24, then drew 1-1 with Fulham on October 31. A positive result at Old Trafford would stretch that run further and reinforce Villa’s case as one of the form teams in the division right now.
Manchester United confirmed lineup
Carrick sets Manchester United up in a 4-2-3-1, with Senne Lammens behind a back line of Diogo Dalot, Leny Yoro, Ayden Heaven and Harry Maguire. Kobbie Mainoo and Youri Tielemans sit as the double pivot, shielding a back four that has shipped goals in each of the last two games. Ahead of them, Bruno Fernandes operates centrally behind Matheus Cunha, flanked by Amad Diallo and Bryan Mbeumo, giving the attack width and combination play through the final third. The team is missing a significant chunk of its squad depth, with Marcus Rashford, Benjamin Šeško, Manuel Ugarte, Lisandro Martínez, Luke Shaw and Patrick Dorgu all out, which limits Carrick’s options both in attack and across the back line.
Manchester United confirmed starting XI (4-2-3-1): Senne Lammens, Leny Yoro, Harry Maguire, Noussair Mazraoui, Diogo Dalot, Kobbie Mainoo, Bruno Fernandes, Youri Tielemans, Amad Diallo, Matheus Cunha, Bryan Mbeumo. Coach: Michael Carrick.
Aston Villa confirmed lineup
Emery mirrors the hosts with a 4-2-3-1, Zion Suzuki starting behind Ian Maatsen, Pau Torres, Victor Lindelöf and Lamare Bogarde. Boubacar Kamara and Johan Manzambi anchor midfield, with Leon Goretzka pushed into a more advanced role. Alysson Edward Alysson and John McGinn support Nicolas Jackson in attack, giving Villa pace and movement to work off the lone striker. Villa are without Matty Cash, Amadou Onana, Matteo Ruggeri and Aaron Wan-Bissaka, which thins out their full back and defensive midfield options, but the rest of the lineup carries the same personnel that has driven their unbeaten run.
Aston Villa confirmed starting XI (4-2-3-1): Zion Suzuki, Taylor Harwood-Bellis, Victor Lindelöf, Pau Torres, Ian Maatsen, Boubacar Kamara, Johan Manzambi, Leon Goretzka, Alysson Edward Alysson, Nicolas Jackson, John McGinn. Coach: Unai Emery.

items.title: Genoa vs AC Milan: Confirmed lineups for the 2026-27 Serie A match
items.description:
Take a look at the projected lineups for Genoa vs AC Milan in the 2026-27 Serie A. Genoa host AC Milan at a moment when both sides arrive full of confidence, and this one has the look of a genuine measuring-stick fixture for the home side.
Genoa have won three straight, beating Lecce 2-1 on November 1 after a 2-0 win over Juventus on October 28 and a 1-0 result against Venezia FC on October 25. That stretch includes a statement win over Juventus, and De Rossi’s side will want to show that was no fluke against another top club. A victory here would extend their run to four games and keep them firmly in the upper half of the table conversation.
AC Milan head into this match off a 3-1 win over Inter on October 31, bouncing back from a 2-4 loss to Bologna on October 28 after beating Udinese 2-0 on October 25. The Inter result shows Milan can still produce big performances even after a setback, and Amorim will be looking for more consistency from his team. Another win on the road would steady the ship and keep Milan’s season on track after that loss to Bologna.
Genoa confirmed lineup
De Rossi sets Genoa up in a 3-4-2-1, with Bijlow behind a back three of Marcandalli, Oestigard and Vásquez. Messias and Ehizibue provide the width as wing-backs, while Frendrup anchors the midfield alongside Traoré. El Shaarawy and Ellertsson sit just behind Osmajić, who leads the line. There are no absences listed for Genoa, so De Rossi can call on his strongest available group for this one.
Genoa confirmed starting XI (3-4-2-1): Justin Bijlow, Alessandro Marcandalli, Leo Ostigard, Johan Vásquez, Júnior Messias, Kingsley Ehizibue, Morten Frendrup, Hamed Junior Traoré, Mikael Ellertsson, Vítor Carvalho, Milutin Osmajić. Coach: Daniele De Rossi.
AC Milan confirmed lineup
Amorim also lines Milan up in a 3-4-2-1, with Maignan in goal behind Gila, De Winter and Bartesaghi. Pulisic and Moreira operate as the wing-backs, with Modrić and Musah controlling the center of the park. Rabiot and Diawara play in support of Ramos up top. Milan have no listed absences, giving Amorim a full squad to pick from as they look to build on their win over Inter.
AC Milan confirmed starting XI (3-4-2-1): Mike Maignan, Mario Gila, Koni De Winter, Alphadjo Cissé, Christian Pulisic, Diego Moreira, Luka Modrić, Yunus Musah, Adrien Rabiot, Sankhoun Diawara, Gonçalo Ramos. Coach: Ruben Amorim.

items.title: Crystal Palace vs Liverpool: Confirmed lineups for the 2026-27 Premier League match
items.description:
Take a look at the projected lineups for Crystal Palace vs Liverpool in the 2026-27 Premier League. Crystal Palace host Liverpool at a difficult moment for both sides, with each team searching for a way to stop a run of results going the wrong way.
Crystal Palace come into this one on a three-game losing streak, falling 0-2 to Tottenham on October 31 after a 0-2 defeat to Newcastle on October 25. Before that they were beaten 0-5 by Albion on October 18, a run that has left them without a win in their last three. This match is a chance to stop the slide before it does more damage to their season.
Liverpool, despite a 0-1 loss to Arsenal on November 1, had won back-to-back matches before that setback, beating Albion 2-0 on October 25 and Brentford 2-1 on October 17. The Arsenal defeat snapped that winning run, and Liverpool will want to show it was a blip rather than a trend. A win at Selhurst Park would steady things quickly.
Crystal Palace confirmed lineup
Pierre Sage sets Crystal Palace up in a 3-4-2-1, with Chris Richards, Axel Disasi and Jaydee Canvot forming the back three in front of Dean Henderson. Adam Wharton and Quinten Timber anchor the midfield, while Daichi Kamada and Anan Khalaili operate just behind Jorgen Strand Larsen, who leads the line. Tyrick Mitchell and Yéremy Pino provide width from wing-back positions. The team is missing Ismaïla Sarr, Jean-Philippe Mateta, Chadi Riad and Takehiro Tomiyasu, a significant group of absences that affects both attacking depth and squad options at the back.
Crystal Palace confirmed starting XI (3-4-2-1): Dean Henderson, Óscar Mingueza, Tyrick Mitchell, Axel Disasi, Chris Richards, Jefferson Lerma, Adam Wharton, Quinten Timber, Jørgen Strand Larsen, Daichi Kamada, Yéremy Pino. Coach: Pierre Sage.
Liverpool confirmed lineup
Andoni Iraola lines Liverpool up in a 4-2-3-1, with Alisson behind a back four of Ronald Araujo, Jérémy Jacquet, Virgil Van Dijk and Miloš Kerkez. Alexis Mac Allister and Treymaurice Nyoni sit in the double pivot, supporting an attacking line of Florian Wirtz, Bradley Barcola and Cody Gakpo behind lone striker Alexander Isak. Liverpool are without Conor Bradley, Jeremie Frimpong, Giovanni Leoni, Amara Nallo and Hugo Ekitiké, a list that includes both first-choice full backs and the senior striker option behind Isak.
Liverpool confirmed starting XI (4-2-3-1): Alisson Becker, Ronald Araujo, Miloš Kerkez, Alexis Mac Allister, Jérémy Jacquet, Virgil van Dijk, Cody Gakpo, Dominik Szoboszlai, Alexander Isak, Florian Wirtz, Bradley Barcola. Coach: Andoni Iraola.

items.title: Kylian Mbappe’s scoring run at Real Madrid puts him on the trail of a Cristiano Ronaldo record
items.description:
Kylian Mbappe’s form with Real Madrid is putting him in the same conversation as Cristiano Ronaldo, with streaks in LaLiga and the Champions League that few players in the club’s history have reached. 
Kylian Mbappe keeps finding the net at the right moments for Real Madrid. On Saturday, the French forward sealed a 3-0 win over Valencia at Mestalla, stretching his tally to 13 LaLiga goals this season and getting closer and closer to an impressive Cristiano Ronaldo record.



According to data shared by football statistics account MisterChip, Mbappe has now scored in seven consecutive games for Real Madrid in all official competitions, and the streak is still alive.



That puts him within reach of a mark that belongs to Cristiano Ronaldo: the Portuguese forward appears twice in the same list with runs of 12 consecutive games with a goal, one in 2014 and another in 2018, the longest among Madrid players with streaks of seven or more in recent years.



The rest of the list shows how few players have gotten close. Mbappe himself reached eight in a row in 2025, while Karim Benzema had two runs of seven, in 2021 and 2022. Ronaldo, on the other hand, dominates the older part of the ranking, with a streak of 10 in 2014, two of eight in 2012 and 2013, and another of seven in 2012.




Mbappé scores (this was a scheduled tweet) ⏰ pic.twitter.com/51OB6dmg9w— Real Madrid C.F. 🇬🇧🇺🇸 (@realmadriden) November 7, 2026




For Mbappe, matching Ronaldo’s 12 would mean scoring in five more consecutive games, and he would need six to pass him. It is a long way to go, but he is the one who has come closest to Ronaldo’s streaks since the Portuguese left the club, and the way he is playing makes it a story worth following in the coming weeks.



A flying start in LaLiga and Europe


        


Mbappe has made scoring look routine in LaLiga. After the win at Mestalla, he has 13 goals and two assists in 12 league matches, trailing only Barcelona’s Raphinha, who stands at the top with 15 goals.



His numbers in the Champions League are just as good. Mbappe has scored in all four of Real Madrid’s league-phase matches, adding one assist, and the run goes back further: his goal against AEK Athens was his sixth in a row in the competition, tying the best streak of his career, set with PSG in 2022.



That Champions League run has put him in the same conversation as Cristiano Ronaldo. Until this week, the Portuguese forward was the only Real Madrid player to have scored in six or more straight matches in the competition, and his mark of 11 will be hard to match. 



With Real Madrid among the title contenders in LaLiga and unbeaten so far in the Champions League, Mbappe has every chance to keep adding to his numbers. Each match gives him another opportunity to extend his runs in Spain and Europe, and to keep moving closer to the marks left by Cristiano Ronaldo.

items.title: Lionel Messi reaches a new personal record with Inter Miami in the regular season finale
items.description:
Lionel Messi’s number for the finale is only part of the story, as the Inter Miami captain also heads into the last day of the regular season with a chance to achieve a pair of firsts that no player has ever managed in the history of MLS. 
Lionel Messi is about to close the 2026 MLS regular season with a mark he had never reached since joining Inter Miami. According to insider José Armando, the captain is set to play his 31st regular-season match of the year against Charlotte FC, the most appearances he has had in a single MLS season with the club.



The previous high was 28 matches in 2025, when Messi scored 29 goals and provided 19 assists on his way to the MLS Golden Boot and the MVP award. This year he arrived at the finale with 30 league appearances, and the MLS Golden Boot tracker had him at 2,574 minutes played, a sign of how much Inter Miami have leaned on their captain throughout a long campaign.



His workload has also come with production. Messi entered the final day at the top of the scoring chart with 26 goals, four more than Dallas forward Petar Musa, and with 14 assists.



The match that will give Messi a personal record also has a lot at stake for Inter Miami in the standings. The team moved into second place after beating New England 2-1 on the road, and a win over Charlotte would guarantee that position, leaving them well placed heading into the playoffs.




VAMOS MIAMI 🩷🖤 pic.twitter.com/3tOTjv7IDt— Inter Miami CF (@InterMiamiCF) November 7, 2026




Messi on the verge of two feats no MLS player has pulled off



Messi’s final day in the regular season could add two more entries to his list of firsts in MLS, starting with the Golden Boot. He enters Decision Day with 26 goals and one more scoring title would make him the first player in the league’s 31-year history to win it in two consecutive seasons.


        


The other milestone within reach is the MVP award. Messi is the main candidate to collect his third in only three full seasons with Inter Miami, which has never been done in MLS. He already has two, and a third would leave him alone at the top of the league’s most prestigious individual honor.



Whatever happens against Charlotte, the focus will soon move to the playoffs, which begin on Nov. 18. If both awards end up in his hands, Messi would finish the year with the kind of double that no one before him has achieved in the league.

items.title: FIFA cuts suspension for Argentina’s Nahuel Molina but keeps Leandro Paredes’ ban over World Cup final incidents
items.description:
Nahuel Molina now has one game left to serve, while Leandro Paredes will be unavailable for Argentina until at least September 2027, and the Argentine Football Association is heading to the Court of Arbitration for Sport to seek a new review of the decision. 
Months after the World Cup final, the incidents that followed Spain’s 1-0 win over Argentina are still making headlines. FIFA’s Appeals Committee ruled on Friday on the appeal filed by the Argentine Football Association (AFA), partially accepting it: Nahuel Molina’s suspension was reduced, but Leandro Paredes’ ban was left untouched.



In Molina’s case, the right back’s suspension went from seven matches to four, while his fine dropped from 90,000 to 60,000 dollars. The national team has already played three games with him suspended, during the October FIFA window against Bolivia, Benin and Burkina Faso, so he has one match left to serve with Argentina.



Paredes did not get the same treatment. FIFA upheld the 10-match suspension and the 90,000-dollar fine that the Disciplinary Committee had imposed on him in August, after his clash with Spanish players Eric Garcia and Gavi following the final.



Of those ten games, three have been served and the midfielder will be unavailable for Argentina at least until September 2027. In August, FIFA also agreed to the AFA’s request that suspended matches be counted in friendlies and official CONMEBOL games.



Leandro Paredes #5 of Argentina and Eric Garcia #4 of Spain have words after the World Cup 2026 Final. (Getty Images)



The AFA also faces penalties and heads to CAS



The ruling was not only about the players. The Appeals Committee also upheld the fines imposed on the AFA over discriminatory chants heard during the tournament, according to the association’s statement.



Those sanctions came from the Disciplinary Committee’s August decision, which included a 321,000-dollar fine and matches with restricted attendance for Argentina, applied after incidents in the team’s games against Cape Verde, Egypt, Switzerland, England and Spain.



The August decision also reached members of the Argentine delegation: Thiago Almada received a one-match suspension, while staff member Roberto Ayala was given a three-match ban.



The AFA said it will now request the grounds for the decisions and take the case to the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS), considering that it has sufficient arguments of fact and law to seek a new review. For now, Paredes’ 10-match suspension and the fines remain in force, while Molina is closer to returning, with one game left to serve.

items.title: Cristiano Ronaldo’s No. 7 Portugal shirt may be in limbo as Rafael Leao suffers injury scare
items.description:
Rafael Leao’s injury scare leaves Portugal’s No. 7 up in the air, and Pedro Neto, Joao Felix and Francisco Trincao are among the names who have worn the number. 
Cristiano Ronaldo’s No. 7 shirt with the Portugal national team may have to wait for its next wearer. A few days after Ronaldo’s retirement from international football, Rafael Leao was forced off injured during Galatasaray’s win over Amedspor, which raises doubts about his availability for the next international window.



On Saturday, in the Turkish Super Lig, Leao opened the scoring in the seventh minute, but in the 50th he went down after a backheel pass, grabbed his right leg and was replaced by Deniz Gul. 



Portuguese outlets such as Record and O Jogo described the problem as a muscle issue in the right thigh, although there is no official diagnosis or recovery timeline yet. The timing is a concern for Portugal, as Jorge Jesus called Leao up for the Nations League games during the international break.



Leao appears to be a candidate to succeed Ronaldo, as the No. 7 has already passed through his hands once. On Oct. 1, ahead of the Nations League match in Denmark, Ronaldo left Portugal’s camp in Copenhagen and the Galatasaray forward wore the No. 7 against Denmark and gave his usual No. 17 to Fabio Silva.




Sempre connosco. Obrigado, Portugueses. ❤️‍🔥 pic.twitter.com/qruLL2zbZ4— Portugal (@selecaoportugal) October 1, 2026




Who else could wear the No. 7?



Leao is not the only Portuguese attacker who is familiar with the number, and other players are also candidates to take the shirt. Pedro Neto wears the No. 7 at Chelsea, a shirt he has kept for 2026-27 after taking it over in 2024-25. For Portugal he currently wears the No. 18, but his style fits what the number has historically asked for.


        


Joao Felix is another candidate who has already worn the No. 7, at Atletico Madrid, although he wears the No. 11 with the national team and is unlikely to change his number.



Francisco Trincao is another name connected to the number, as he wears it for Al Ahli. Reports from Portugal also mention two younger options: Geovany Quenda, the Chelsea signing who still has to make his debut for the senior team, and Rodrigo Mora, the 19-year-old Roma midfielder who has been called up but has not played for the senior side yet.



For now, there is no official decision on who will carry the shirt that Cristiano Ronaldo wore for 23 years. The symbolism will always remain tied to the legendary forward, but because UEFA requires squads in league-phase Nations League matches to be numbered from 1 to 23, Portugal will have to name someone to wear it.

items.title: Inter Miami vs Charlotte FC: Confirmed lineups for the 2026 MLS season match
items.description:
Take a look at the projected lineups for Inter Miami vs Charlotte FC in the 2026 MLS season. Lionel Messi is listed in the projected Inter Miami lineup for this one, giving the home side their most dangerous attacking option against a Charlotte FC side that has been scoring freely of late.
Inter Miami arrive off a 2-1 win over New England on November 2, but that followed a 2-2 draw with FC Cincinnati on October 28 and a 0-2 loss to the Red Bulls on October 24. The mixed run leaves Kily González searching for consistency rather than just a result. A win here would settle some of that uncertainty and keep Inter Miami’s season on an upward track.
Charlotte FC come in with real momentum, having beaten Orlando City 4-0 on October 31 and CF Montreal by the same scoreline on October 28. Those two blowout wins followed a 2-3 loss to the Timbers on October 25, so Dean Smith’s team has responded well since that setback. A strong showing in Miami would confirm Charlotte FC as one of the league’s form teams heading into the final stretch.
Inter Miami confirmed lineup
Kily González sets Inter Miami up in a 4-3-3 with Dayne St. Clair behind a back four of Gonzalo Luján, Casemiro, Micael and Sergio Reguilón. Casemiro’s presence alongside Rodrigo De Paul and Yannick Bright gives the midfield experience and control, with Matías Galarza offering another option in the middle. Up front, Lionel Messi and Luis Suárez lead the line with Riquelme Fillipi, and there are no listed absences to complicate González’s selection.

items.title: Valencia vs Real Madrid: Confirmed lineups for the 2026-27 LaLiga match
items.description:
Take a look at the projected lineups for Valencia vs Real Madrid in the 2026-27 LaLiga. Valencia host a Real Madrid side riding a wave of attacking form at Mestalla, with Mourinho’s men looking to make it four straight wins and the home side needing a response after a mixed run of results.
Valencia come into this one having won 1-0 against Elche on November 1, a result that followed a 1-2 loss to Villarreal on October 24 and a scoreless draw with Athletic on October 17. The form is uneven, with one win, one loss and one draw across those three games. A positive result here would steady things after that dip against Villarreal and give Aguirre’s side something to build on at home.
Real Madrid arrive off the back of a 3-0 win over Santander on November 1, which came after back-to-back victories over Barcelona 2-1 on October 25 and Sevilla 4-1 on October 18. Three wins in three outings has Madrid scoring freely and traveling with real momentum. Another result in Valencia would keep Mourinho’s side firmly in control of their title push.
Valencia confirmed lineup
Aguirre sets Valencia up in a 3-4-2-1, with Dimitrievski behind a back three of Tárrega, De Haas and a central presence anchored by Pepelu alongside Guido Rodríguez in midfield. Rioja and Maffeo provide width as wing-backs, while Danjuma and Gayà operate just behind Sadiq as the central striker. The lineup is without José Manuel Arias Copete, Sergi Canós, David Otorbi and Diego López, all ruled out, which limits Aguirre’s options in attack and across the squad depth.
Valencia confirmed starting XI (5-3-2): Stole Dimitrievski, Pablo Maffeo, José Gayà, Justin de Haas, César Tárrega, Pepelu, Javi Guerra, Guido Rodríguez, Arnaut Danjuma, Umar Sadiq, Aaron Mayol. Coach: Javier Aguirre.
Real Madrid confirmed lineup
Mourinho lines Real Madrid up in a 4-2-3-1, with Courtois in goal behind a back four of Valverde, Konaté, Huijsen and Cucurella. Tchouaméni and Bellingham sit in the double pivot, with Bernardo Silva, Arda Güler and Yan Diomande supporting Mbappé in the forward line. The absences of Ferland Mendy, Raúl Asencio, Rodrygo and Vinícius Júnior are notable, with Mourinho reshuffling his attacking options and turning to Diomande and Bernardo Silva to carry the creative load alongside Mbappé.
Real Madrid confirmed starting XI (4-2-3-1): Thibaut Courtois, Federico Valverde, Marc Cucurella, Aurélien Tchouaméni, Ibrahima Konaté, Dean Huijsen, Arda Güler, Bernardo Silva, Kylian Mbappé, Jude Bellingham, Yan Diomande. Coach: José Mário dos Santos Mourinho Félix.

items.title: Arsenal vs Hull: Confirmed lineups for the 2026-27 Premier League match
items.description:
Take a look at the projected lineups for Arsenal vs Hull in the 2026-27 Premier League. Arsenal host Hull with the gap between the two clubs on full display before a ball is even kicked, and the team sheets only confirm it.
Arsenal arrive on the back of three straight wins, beating Liverpool 1-0 on November 1 after a 2-0 win over Everton on October 24 and a 1-0 result against Nottingham on October 18. The clean sheets have piled up alongside the goals, and Mikel Arteta’s side look settled and confident. A fourth consecutive win would stretch that run and keep the pressure on anyone chasing them at the top.
Hull come into this one without a win in their last three outings, drawing 2-2 with Ipswich Town on October 31 and 1-1 with Brentford on October 25 after a 0-1 loss to Fulham on October 17. The draws at least show some resistance, but Sergej Jakirović’s side have not found a way to close games out. Three points at the Emirates would be a major statement, but even a point would count as a solid return against this opponent.
Arsenal confirmed lineup
Arteta sets Arsenal up in a 4-2-3-1 with David Raya behind a back four of Jurriën Timber, Ezri Konsa, Gabriel Magalhães and Riccardo Calafiori. Declan Rice and Bruno Guimarães sit in front of them, giving the team control in midfield, while Martín Odegaard operates just ahead in support of Kai Havertz up top. Noni Madueke and Christos Tzolis provide width and pace on the flanks. The absences of Bukayo Saka and William Saliba are notable, along with Louie Copley and Max Dowman also out, but the depth on show suggests Arsenal are well equipped to cope.
Arsenal confirmed starting XI (4-2-3-1): David Raya, Jurriën Timber, Riccardo Calafiori, Bruno Guimarães, Ezri Konsa, Gabriel Magalhães, Noni Madueke, Declan Rice, Kai Havertz, Martin Ødegaard, Christos Tzolis. Coach: Mikel Arteta.
Hull confirmed lineup
Jakirović goes with a defensive 5-4-1 shape, built around a back five of Lewie Coyle, Semi Ajayi, John Egan, Nobel Mendy and Ryan Giles protecting goalkeeper Konstantinos Tzolakis. Mohamed Belloumi, Tim Iroegbunam, Regan Slater and Elliot Stroud make up a packed midfield four tasked with limiting the space Arsenal’s attackers can work in. Oli McBurnie leads the line alone, relying on quick counters to create any threat. Hull are missing a long list of players including Matthew Targett, Eliot Matazo, Charlie Hughes, Jack Butland, Lucas Gourna-Douath, Ilyas Ansah, Darko Gyabi and Sorba Thomas, which explains the cautious setup and the emphasis on numbers behind the ball.
Hull confirmed starting XI (5-3-2): Konstantinos Tzolakis, Lewie Coyle, Elliot Stroud, Nobel Mendy, John Egan, Semi Ajayi, Tim Iroegbunam, Lucas Gourna-Douath, Oliver McBurnie, Mohamed-Ali Cho, Regan Slater. Coach: Sergej Jakirović.

items.title: Leeds vs Tottenham: Confirmed lineups for the 2026-27 Premier League match
items.description:
Take a look at the projected lineups for Leeds vs Tottenham in the 2026-27 Premier League. Leeds and Tottenham arrive at this one going in opposite directions, and that contrast should shape how the game is played out.
Leeds have gone three games without a win, losing 0-2 to Bournemouth on October 31 after draws with Sunderland and Man U. The 0-0 with Sunderland on October 25 followed a 1-1 share of the points with Man U on October 18, and neither result did much to settle any nerves at Elland Road. A home game against one of the league’s form sides is a tough way to try to snap out of it.
Tottenham could hardly be in better shape, winning three straight without conceding, including a 2-0 win over Crystal Palace on October 31. Before that they beat Chelsea 2-0 on October 24 and put three past Coventry on October 19 in a 3-1 win. A fourth consecutive victory would send a strong message that Tottenham belong among the league’s top sides this season.
Leeds confirmed lineup
Daniel Farke sets Leeds up in a 3-4-2-1, with Dominic Calvert-Lewin as the focal point up front and Brenden Aaronson and Harry Wilson tasked with supplying him from deeper positions. Ethan Ampadu and Ao Tanaka anchor the midfield, giving the side some control before the ball is worked out to wing-backs Jayden Bogle and Gabriel Gudmundsson. Leeds are without Noah Okafor, Joe Rodon and Mateo Joseph, which thins out both the forward line and central defensive cover, with Nico Elvedi and Tarik Muharemović left to marshal the back three in Rodon’s absence.
Leeds confirmed starting XI (3-4-2-1): James Trafford, Nico Elvedi, Tarik Muharemović, James Justin, Jayden Bogle, Lukas Nmecha, Ethan Ampadu, Sean Longstaff, Gabriel Gudmundsson, Ao Tanaka, Dominic Calvert-Lewin. Coach: Daniel Farke.
Tottenham confirmed lineup
Roberto De Zerbi lines Tottenham up in a 4-2-3-1, with Mathys Tel leading the line and Mohammed Kudus, James Maddison and Omar Marmoush working in support behind him. Sandro Tonali and Mateus Fernandes sit in front of the back four, screening a defense that includes Micky van de Ven and Jan-Paul van Hecke in the middle. The absentee list is long, with Tosin Adarabioyo, Lucas Bergvall, Wilson Odobert, Mykhaylo Mudryk, Savinho, Xavi Simons, Rodrigo Bentancur and Richarlison all out, but the players coming in have kept the team winning regardless.
Tottenham confirmed starting XI (4-2-3-1): Antonín Kinský, Pedro Porro, Jan-Paul van Hecke, Micky van de Ven, Andy Robertson, Sandro Tonali, Archie Gray, Mateus Fernandes, Mohammed Kudus, Omar Marmoush, Mathys Tel. Coach: Roberto De Zerbi.

items.title: Rise of the ‘schooligans’: how a wave of antisocial behaviour threatens non-league football
items.description: Teenage ultras are increasingly causing disorder and communities fear it will not be long before it becomes something more dangerousIt is five past three on Saturday afternoon and the teenage ultras of Hednesford Town are running late. They have arrived in Chester for their team’s National League North fixture and have hailed taxis, determined to make their presence felt at the ground. But word appears to have got out about their arrival. As one car turns away from the city’s charming half-timbered houses and into narrow residential streets, half a dozen local youths appear, haring round the corner in balaclavas. They try to attack the cab and chase after it as it pulls away. The smell of pyro is everywhere. As the taxi finally gets clear, the Chester gang stops in the middle of the road, shouting and gesticulating. One lad, no older than 16, pulls a long blade from inside his trousers and brandishes it.The incident ended there and no one was hurt, though a police investigation has been launched. The match went off without trouble too and the Hednesford gang – known at home as the “schooligans” – were escorted safely back to the station by Cheshire police. It was just another weekend in English non-league football, where a wave of antisocial behaviour is causing concern and leading the UK Football Policing Unit (UKFPU) to declare it its “most important” priority. As the disorder continues, a question remains: how long will it be before teenage trouble-making becomes something more dangerous? Continue reading...

items.title: Lionel Messi’s Inter Miami confirm two absences for the regular season finale vs Charlotte
items.description:
Lionel Messi’s Inter Miami close the regular season against Charlotte with a growing injury list and a playoff position still at stake. 
Lionel Messi’s Inter Miami will close the 2026 MLS regular season without some of their young defenders. The Herons host Charlotte FC on Saturday at Nu Stadium in the last match before the playoffs, and the injury list has grown.



According to Inter Miami insider Jose Armando, Fricio Caicedo and Cesar Abadia are confirmed absences for the match. Caicedo, an 18-year-old Ecuadorian defender who joined on loan, is dealing with a knee problem, while Abadia’s absence has not been detailed.



The pair join two other players who will not be available either. Tadeo Allende and Mateo Silvetti have been ruled out for the rest of the season. The former Celta Vigo forward underwent arthroscopic surgery on his right knee in Barcelona and is listed with a season-ending injury on the club’s website.



On the other hand, the former Newell’s Old Boys forward, who recorded three goals and four assists in 14 MLS games before getting hurt, underwent surgery on his left shoulder after dislocating it, and the club said he will now focus on his recovery ahead of next season.




Back home. One last regular season showdown. 🏠⚽🔗 https://t.co/TaiIUx6Nzi pic.twitter.com/zkKNeexxto— Inter Miami CF (@InterMiamiCF) November 4, 2026




Despite the absences, coach Kily Gonzalez otherwise has a relatively healthy squad. The team already secured its place in the postseason, with second place in the Eastern Conference still at stake, while Messi, who arrives with 26 goals, four ahead of Petar Musa, will try to clinch his second straight Golden Boot.



Inter Miami’s possible playoff rivals


        


Inter Miami will finish the regular season either second or third in the Eastern Conference. The Herons hold second place with 59 points, one more than New England Revolution, which visits Orlando City at the same time Miami hosts Charlotte. A win against Charlotte guarantees second place, while a draw would be enough unless New England wins.



If Miami ends up second, it will face the seventh seed in Round One. Today that spot belongs to FC Cincinnati, which has 46 points and hosts Nashville SC, but Philadelphia Union (47), Columbus Crew (44) and Orlando City (43) are all in the race for the last direct spot, so the rival could change.



If Miami finishes third, it will meet the sixth seed, currently Philadelphia Union with 47 points and a home match against Toronto FC. Cincinnati and Columbus could also climb to that position, which means Miami’s opponent will not be known until all matches end at the same time on Saturday.

items.title: Lionel Messi chases two unprecedented MLS records on the final day of the regular season
items.description:
Lionel Messi enters the final day of the MLS regular season with two chances to rewrite history: a record-breaking scoring title and a third MVP award. 
Lionel Messi has made a habit of breaking barriers in Major League Soccer, but the final day of the 2026 regular season could add two more entries to his collection. At 39 years old, the Inter Miami captain heads into the last matchday with a chance to achieve two feats that no player has accomplished in the league’s 31 years of history.



The first one is the Golden Boot. Messi arrives at the final match with 26 goals, four more than his closest pursuer, Dallas forward Petar Musa, and with the chance to become the first player in MLS history to win two consecutive scoring titles.



Several players have won the award more than once, among them Preki, Taylor Twellman, Jeff Cunningham, Chris Wondolowski and Bradley Wright-Phillips, but none has done it in back-to-back seasons.



The Argentine has been at the center of Inter Miami’s season once again. In 30 league matches, he has scored 26 goals and provided 14 assists, numbers that make him the main candidate for the individual awards this year.




Simplemente Leo Messi. 🔟 ✨ pic.twitter.com/sqiH0DzCef— Inter Miami CF (@InterMiamiCF) November 2, 2026




Inter Miami closes the regular season on Saturday against Charlotte FC, and Messi will have one last chance to extend his advantage over Musa. If the Dallas striker does not close the gap, the Golden Boot will go back to the Argentine, and with it a record that has eluded some of the best scorers in the league’s history.



A third MVP in three seasons


        


The second record is the MVP award. Messi is the main candidate to win his third Most Valuable Player award in three full seasons with Inter Miami, something that no player has achieved in MLS history. He already holds two, and with a third he would stand alone in the history of the league’s most prestigious individual honor.



Beyond his numbers, the Inter Miami star has kept the team among the top contenders in the East, a combination of impact and consistency that has defined each of his MVP-caliber campaigns since he arrived in 2023.



The regular season ends this weekend, but the story will continue through the playoffs, which begin on Nov. 18. For Messi, the chance to leave his mark twice in the same year, with a second Golden Boot and a third MVP, would only strengthen a legacy in American soccer that no one has been able to match.

items.title: Cristiano Ronaldo reportedly drops Al-Nassr exit bombshell after Portugal retirement as potential final appearance date emerges
items.description:
The Portuguese superstar is reportedly considering bringing his time in Saudi Arabia to an end, although the club hierarchy is determined to keep him in Riyadh. 
Cristiano Ronaldo could be approaching another major turning point in his career, with reports suggesting that his future at Al-Nassr is becoming increasingly uncertain following his retirement from international soccer. The Portuguese superstar is reportedly considering bringing his time in Saudi Arabia to an end, although the club hierarchy is determined to keep him in Riyadh.



At 41, Ronaldo remains one of Al-Nassr‘s most important players, both on and off the pitch. However, speculation surrounding his next move has intensified, with reports indicating that the 2026-27 campaign could represent the final chapter of his spell at the Saudi giant.



The latest speculation comes shortly after the 41-year-old announced his retirement from Portugal on November 5, 2026. He ended his international career with 234 appearances and 146 goals, leaving behind a record that made him the highest-scoring player in men’s international soccer. His decision means he can now concentrate entirely on club soccer without the demands of international breaks.



Under coach Ange Postecoglou, Al-Nassr will hope to benefit from his continued availability as the club pursues domestic and continental honors. Ronaldo is also approaching another extraordinary individual milestone. Following a hat-trick in Al-Nassr’s 5-3 victory over Al Kholood on October 29, he reached 985 official career goals, leaving him 15 short of the 1,000-goal target.



Ronaldo's hat-trick to take him to goal 985 🤩 pic.twitter.com/oxgu7aqua2— Roshn Saudi League (@SPL_EN) October 29, 2026 



The possibility of retirement has already been discussed by the forward himself. In an August 2026 interview with Vogue, he described the ongoing campaign as “probably my last year of football”, while expressing his desire to leave behind a remarkable legacy.



Ronaldo’s Al-Nassr future takes dramatic turn



According to 365Scores, Ronaldo has informed Al-Nassr officials that the ongoing season could be his last with the club. The report claims that the hierarchy is keen to extend his contract beyond its current expiration date in June 2027.



Al-Nassr is reportedly exploring ways to persuade the forward to remain for another season, while also considering how to honor his contribution if he decides to leave. A potential farewell match and a major celebration are among the plans being discussed, although neither Ronaldo’s departure nor any formal tribute has been confirmed.



Since arriving in Riyadh in early 2023, the Portuguese ace has helped transform the Knight of Najd’s international profile and attracted considerable attention to Saudi soccer. He also played a major role in the club’s reported 2025-26 Saudi Pro League title triumph, scoring 28 league goals during the campaign.



Cristiano Ronaldo of Al Nassr celebrates with the Saudi Pro League Trophy.



When could Ronaldo make his final professional appearance?



While Ronaldo has yet to confirm whether he intends to retire after the current campaign, speculation has also emerged about when his final professional appearance could take place.



According to the official Saudi Pro League schedule, May 28, 2027, could become the date of Ronaldo’s final match if he decides to retire at the end of the season. The suggested occasion is particularly significant, as Ange Postecoglou’s players are scheduled to face fierce Riyadh rival Al-Hilal in the final round of the Saudi Pro League.



Cristiano Ronaldo of Al Nassr is challenged by Nasser Al-Dawsari of Al Hilal.



The potential farewell would take place at Kingdom Arena, Al-Hilal’s home ground, giving Ronaldo the opportunity to end his career in one of Saudi Arabia’s biggest soccer rivalries. However, this remains an early speculative prediction rather than a confirmed retirement plan or official announcement.



For now, Al-Nassr is still hoping to convince their captain to extend his stay, and Ronaldo has several months remaining on his current contract. Whether he signs a new deal, pursues another challenge, or retires after reaching 1,000 goals remains uncertain, but his next decision could determine how one of soccer’s most remarkable careers comes to a close.

items.title: Jose Mourinho believes Cristiano Ronaldo’s career is far from over after Portugal national team retirement
items.description:
José Mourinho, who coached Cristiano Ronaldo at Real Madrid, says the forward’s career is not over despite his Portugal retirement, and that those who know him are aware he still has goals. 
Cristiano Ronaldo’s farewell from the Portugal national team has drawn reactions from across the soccer world, and one of the most anticipated came from a man who knows him better than most. Jose Mourinho, who coached Ronaldo for three seasons at Real Madrid (2010-2013), was asked about the news on Friday, a day after the forward announced the end of his international career.



Speaking at his press conference ahead of Real Madrid’s LaLiga trip to Valencia, Mourinho first made clear that he did not want to dwell on the decision itself. “His decision must be respected, and I do respect it,” he said, before adding that he does not see it as a full retirement. “It is not retirement,” the Portuguese coach explained, drawing a line between the end of Ronaldo’s time with the national team and the rest of his career.



“He hasn’t ended his career, those who know him are aware that he still has goals,” Mourinho continued, before sharing a wish tied to the timing of the announcement: “The only thing I would like is for his retirement as a footballer to be on a different day than yesterday”.



His words carry extra weight given where Ronaldo stands today. The forward remains Al Nassr’s top scorer this season and is under contract with the club until 2027. He is also coming off a hat trick that took him to 985 career goals, just 15 short of the historic 1,000, and Mourinho appears to understand that Ronaldo’s story is still being written, even after leaving his international duty.



Mourinho: "Gostaria que a retirada de Cristiano Ronaldo como jogador de futebol, quando chegar esse dia, seja um dia diferente do dia de ontem" pic.twitter.com/BfgQsEzTQU— Cabine Desportiva (@CabineSport) November 6, 2026 



Could Ronaldo become a coach after retirement?



Mourinho was also asked whether he could picture Ronaldo following his path into coaching one day, but the Portuguese coach chose not to look that far ahead. “If I see him as a coach, I can’t say, I don’t know what may go through his head. It’s too early to even comment. He’s still a football player,” he said.


        


The answer reflects the same idea that ran through the rest of his comments: for Mourinho, Ronaldo’s retirement from Portugal is a closed chapter with the national team, not a step toward life after soccer. Speaking about his former player in the present tense, the coach made clear that the conversation about what comes next can wait.



For now, Ronaldo has plenty left to do on the pitch. The forward is defending the Saudi Pro League title he won last season, with Al Nassr currently third in the table,  and his next test comes on Nov. 20 against Al Qadsiah. Whether he ends up on the bench someday remains an open question, but those who know him, as Mourinho said, are well aware that he still has goals.

items.title: Why Cristiano Ronaldo’s Al-Nassr won’t play today against Al-Hazem in 2026-27 Saudi Pro League
items.description:
The forward was expected to feature for Al-Nassr on Friday, November 6, as the club prepared to visit Al-Hazem in the 2026-27 Saudi Pro League, only for the fixture to disappear from the schedule. 
Cristiano Ronaldo has brought his international career with Portugal to an end, but his return to club soccer has encountered an unexpected delay. The forward was expected to feature for Al-Nassr on Friday, November 6, as the club prepared to visit Al-Hazem in the 2026-27 Saudi Pro League, only for the fixture to disappear from the schedule.



The postponement comes at a significant moment for Ronaldo, who is closing in on one of soccer’s most remarkable individual milestones. With his next appearance now pushed back, supporters will have to wait longer to see him continue his pursuit of 1,000 career goals.



The postponement temporarily interrupts Ronaldo’s pursuit of the 1,000-goal milestone. The Portuguese forward currently has 985 official senior career goals, leaving him just 15 away from a landmark no player has previously reached in official senior matches.



He moved closer to the target with a hat-trick in Al-Nassr’s 5-3 victory over Al-Kholood on October 29. The 41-year-old subsequently missed the club’s 6-2 AFC Champions League victory over Uzbek side Pakhtakor on November 2, having been rested for the match.



Ronaldo's hat-trick to take him to goal 985 🤩 pic.twitter.com/oxgu7aqua2— Roshn Saudi League (@SPL_EN) October 29, 2026 



Ronaldo also announced his retirement from international soccer on November 5, ending a 23-year career with Portugal. He leaves the national team as its record appearance-maker and leading goalscorer, with 234 caps and 146 goals.



Why was Al-Nassr vs. Al-Hazem postponed?



The Saudi Pro League announced on Tuesday, November 3, that all Matchweek 13 fixtures in the 2026-27 season would be postponed. Al-Nassr’s scheduled meeting with Al-Hazem was among the affected games, and no replacement date has been confirmed. The decision followed the Asian Football Confederation’s announcement that the 2027 AFC Asian Cup had been rescheduled. 



The tournament, which Saudi Arabia is due to host, was initially planned for January 7 to February 5, 2027, but will now take place from December 23, 2027, to January 21, 2028, amid security concerns following attacks in the kingdom. The revised continental competition dates have created additional flexibility in the domestic soccer calendar, prompting the league to reconsider how its remaining fixtures should be distributed.



The Saudi Pro League explained: “The decision comes as part of a wider review of the 2026-27 RSL (Roshn Saudi League) fixture schedule, with the revised Asian Cup dates creating additional flexibility in the domestic football calendar.”



Cristiano Ronaldo of Al Nassr.



The league also stressed that the review would prioritize player welfare and a more balanced schedule, adding that it would organize a workshop with participating clubs to discuss proposed adjustments and collect feedback before finalizing the new calendar. “The review will focus on achieving a more balanced distribution of fixtures across the remainder of the season, while ensuring adequate rest and recovery periods for players,” the statement continued.



Al-Nassr will therefore not receive a defeat or lose points because of the postponement. The entire round has been rescheduled, meaning the clubs involved will retain their existing points until their matches are played.



When is Cristiano Ronaldo’s next game?



With the Al-Hazem fixture postponed and Ronaldo no longer expected to represent Portugal during the upcoming international window, his next scheduled opportunity to return is Al-Nassr’s meeting with Al-Qadsiah on November 20, 2026.



Al Hilal become the first team to hit 30 points this season 🔝 https://t.co/xOVgOndql4— Roshn Saudi League (@SPL_EN) October 31, 2026




The Matchday 14 encounter is expected to take place at Al-Awwal Park in Riyadh, although the kick-off time has not been confirmed. Al-Nassr entered the postponed Matchweek 13 in third place with 28 points, having accumulated those points across its first 11 league matches.



The club will now have additional time to prepare for its next domestic assignment, while the league works with its teams to finalize the revised schedule. For Ronaldo, the wait also means a little more time before he can resume his pursuit of the historic 1,000-goal mark.

items.title: Jorge Jesus has no regrets over the Cristiano Ronaldo situation: ‘I wouldn’t change anything’
items.description:
A day after Cristiano Ronaldo announced his retirement from the Portugal national team, Jorge Jesus faced the question that hung over the Portuguese camp: would he have done anything differently? The head coach answered in his first press conference since the announcement, held on Friday at the Cidade do Futebol, where he also revealed his […] 
A day after Cristiano Ronaldo announced his retirement from the Portugal national team, Jorge Jesus faced the question that hung over the Portuguese camp: would he have done anything differently? The head coach answered in his first press conference since the announcement, held on Friday at the Cidade do Futebol, where he also revealed his squad for Portugal’s final two Nations League group games.



Asked if he would change anything about how he handled the situation with Ronaldo, Jesus left no room for doubt. “I wouldn’t change anything, absolutely nothing. I made a decision as a coach, putting the interests of my team and the Portuguese national team first,” he said. He added that he is “convinced” he did not do anything to cause what happened, and described himself as “perfectly calm” about his decision.



The coach also explained how he experienced the news. Jesus said he learned of Ronaldo’s decision at the same time as everyone, following the video and statement the forward published, and that until then he had no knowledge of his intention to leave.



He even revealed that Ronaldo was among the players he was considering for the squad. “If I just said I was thinking of calling him up, it’s because I believed Cristiano Ronaldo would continue with this Nations League project. There are no hard feelings,” Jesus explained. He did acknowledge, however, that the dispute between the two may have rushed things.



"NÃO MUDAVA NADA, ZERO." pic.twitter.com/rKUUxL8C5H— B24 (@B24PT) November 6, 2026 



Jesus closes the chapter and looks ahead



Jesus had no interest in letting the Ronaldo debate take over the rest of the week. After answering several questions about the forward’s departure, the coach tried to close the subject and turn the page toward what comes next. “This subject has already been addressed and I’m not going to talk about it again. That topic is closed,” he said, while insisting that he must respect Ronaldo’s decision.


        


His message was also directed at the squad. Jesus said it is time to talk about the group and the new players, and noted that the captain’s armband will go to one of the team’s most experienced players: Bernardo Silva, Bruno Fernandes, Ruben Dias, Joao Cancelo and Ruben Neves, the five with the most appearances, according to the coach.



With that in mind, the coach’s focus shifts to a squad that faces Denmark on Nov. 14 in Braga and Wales on Nov. 17, and to a new era without the player who defined the national team for 23 years.



Portugal’s squad for UEFA Nations League games



Jesus announced a 28-player squad for the final two group games, with Ronaldo’s absence being the biggest change.



Goalkeepers: Diogo Costa (Porto), Rui Silva (Sporting), Samuel Soares (Benfica).



Defenders: Diogo Dalot (Manchester United), Alberto Costa (Porto), Ruben Dias (Manchester City), Tomas Araujo (Benfica), Renato Veiga (Villarreal), Antonio Silva (Bournemouth), Joao Cancelo (Barcelona), Nuno Tavares (Lazio).



Midfielders: Joao Palhinha (Benfica), Ruben Neves (Al-Hilal), Mateus Fernandes (Tottenham), Vitinha (Paris Saint-Germain), Joao Neves (Paris Saint-Germain), Bernardo Silva (Real Madrid), Pedro Neto (Chelsea), Francisco Trincao (Al-Ahli), Bruno Fernandes (Manchester United).



Forwards: Carlos Forbs (Club Brugge), Joao Felix (Al-Nassr), Rafael Leao (Galatasaray), Geovany Quenda (Chelsea), Rodrigo Mora (Roma), Goncalo Ramos (AC Milan), Fabio Silva (Borussia Dortmund), Gustavo Varela (Monza).

items.title: Football Daily | You want proper football? Here are the FA Cup first-round ties to look out for
items.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now!For the FA Cup, the early rounds are the juice. The first round proper to be played out over the long weekend is looking, well, proper. And on Saturday at 3pm GMT, a proper time, 31 ties will kick off. No VAR, either. At the stage when the bottom two Football League divisions join the competition, focus remains on those non-league clubs fighting for the honour of the pyramid …John Aloisi winning or choking​ the Chinese Super League, a league so ‘super’ that nine of all 16 clubs in it started the season on negative points due to ‘match-fixing, gambling and corruption’ by the way, and the league leaders not even scoring a single goal in seven hours, is really not something to lay upon someone with a bad hangover. Apropos of nothing, if anyone has any objections to my views on the Chinese Super League, please address any correspondence to: Mr K Mbappé, Madrid (there’s no point two of us getting into trouble)” – Noble Francis.As a man of a certain age frequently being reminded of how out of date I am, the recent readers’ letters regarding technical solutions to shirt-pulling (Football Daily letters passim) concerns triggered distant memories. In late 1991 I was working in the Patents Advice Centre, Newcastle Central Library. A gentleman asked for help to possibly patent an ‘invention’: a football shirt with the seams held together by Velcro, so that any tug would ‘open’ the seam and provide clear evidence to the referee of illegal cloth gathering. As I helped him search for possible equivalent innovations in our paper database (yes kids!) we chatted amiably until I asked how he had come to this seemingly simple yet brilliant innovation. He paused, reddened and began to exhale with elevated pressure: ‘Did you see Arsenal the other night? Tony Adams? Disgraceful. It should never be allowed! In fact, with this shirt it won’t be, and Arsenal will have to learn to defend decently!’ Happy memories, obviously irrelavant to the modern game” – Garren Mulloy.Not fair! Bias! (Picture me, arms wide out, mouth open, eyebrows as high as they’ll go, appealing for reason.) I wrote about skin-tight shirts the other day and you ignored it, publishing a Velcro alternative. Now you’ve published another letter about skin-tight shirts (yesterday’s letters), days later. And it gets letter o’ the day! What’s the literary equivalent of kicking the keeper’s water bottle in frustration? I’ve just done that” – Ken Muir.I see that Celtic finally moved up the Bigger Vase charts on Thursday night and started playing a tune when their subs Osmand, Durán and Donovan came on. Too corny but my wife actually laughed at this” – Hugh Jamieson.That was a topsy-turvy Durán Durán show at Celtic, but what else would you expect from a bunch of Wild Bhoys?” – Peter Oh.This is an extract from our daily football email … Football Daily. To get the full version, just visit this page and follow the instructions.  Continue reading...

items.title: Cristiano Ronaldo leaves behind two nearly unbreakable records after retiring from Portugal
items.description:
Cristiano Ronaldo’s farewell from Portugal leaves behind two numbers that no active player is close to challenging. 
Cristiano Ronaldo has closed a 23-year international career that took him from a teenager replacing Luis Figo in a friendly to the greatest figure in Portugal’s history. His retirement, announced on Thursday, leaves behind a legacy of titles and unforgettable moments, but also two records that look more out of reach than ever, in men’s international soccer worldwide. The question now is whether anyone can ever get close.



The first is the goals record, in which the striker is the all-time top scorer for a national team. Ronaldo finished with 146 for Portugal, a total built over more than two decades that he kept growing until his final World Cup, where he scored his last international goal from the penalty spot against Croatia in the round of 32. The record has been his since 2021, when two goals against the Republic of Ireland took him to 111 and past Iran’s Ali Daei, who held it with 109.



The gap he leaves is enormous. Lionel Messi, the closest player on the list, ended his Argentina career with 126 goals, 20 fewer than Ronaldo, and since he retired in October after his farewell match against Benin, that total will not grow. Daei is long retired, and so is India’s Sunil Chhetri, who sits fourth on the list with 95 goals.



That leaves the active players with a mountain to climb. Belgium’s Romelu Lukaku, 33, has 94 goals and Poland’s Robert Lewandowski, 38, has 92, which puts both more than 50 goals short of Ronaldo. Given their ages, it is hard to imagine either of them catching up, and no one else is close enough to threaten the record.




Uma história que fica para sempre. 𝙊𝙗𝙧𝙞𝙜𝙖𝙙𝙤 𝙥𝙤𝙧 𝙩𝙪𝙙𝙤, 𝘾𝙖𝙥𝙞𝙩𝙖̃𝙤 🐐⭐️ pic.twitter.com/OSKr7L7xMW— Portugal (@selecaoportugal) November 5, 2026




234 caps: a mark that may be even harder to reach



The appearances record tells a similar story. Ronaldo finished with 234 caps for Portugal, a figure that makes him the most-capped player in the history of men’s international soccer. He broke the previous record of 196, held by Kuwait’s Bader Al-Mutawa, in 2023, and he was the first player to reach 200 appearances, a milestone he hit against Iceland in a Euro 2024 qualifier.


        


Behind him, the list is shorter on active players than it looks. Messi finished second with 208 caps, 26 fewer than Ronaldo, but he has already retired. The only name in the top five who could still add to his total is third-placed Luka Modric, with 206 caps for Croatia. At 41 years old, however, he would need more than 30 additional appearances to challenge Ronaldo, something that looks highly unlikely.



In the end, both records speak of the same thing: longevity and consistency at the highest level. To catch Ronaldo, a player would have to score at an elite rate and stay on the national team for more than two decades, without serious injuries or a drop in form. 



With Messi, Daei and the rest of the list already gone, and the active names far behind, the numbers that Ronaldo leaves behind, 146 goals and 234 caps, may stand for generations.

items.description: Only 3,587 people live in his family’s village but the streets of Navahermosa were fuller yet quieter to mourn the Tenerife striker at his funeralThe narrow streets of Navahermosa in La Mancha were fuller than they have ever been on Thursday afternoon and quieter too. Silence accompanied the funeral cortege as its made way from the funeral home to the parish church of San Miguel Arcángel carrying Jesús de Miguel Alameda, “Demi”, the Tenerife striker who died after an on-field collision with the Andorra goalkeeper Jesús Owono three days earlier. Only 3,587 people live in his family’s village but now they were joined by the game he loved. “We wanted to be close to his parents, his wife and daughter. In moments of pain, football comes together more than ever,” said Luis de la Fuente.The Spain manager did not say much else; there was not much else he could say, not much anyone could. These have been dark, desperate days, days when it was impossible to assimilate what has happened, and there will be more. “We will get through this together but we will need help, professional help,” the Tenerife president, Felipe Miñambres, said. items.title: Argentina won’t use Lionel Messi’s No.10 jersey in the next window: Can they retire it for official competitions?
items.description:
With Lionel Messi gone, Argentina’s most iconic number has no owner for now, and head coach Lionel Scaloni has reportedly decided that no one will wear it in the next FIFA window. 
Argentina is preparing for a different kind of international window. Lionel Messi has stepped away from the national team after a farewell match against Benin, and with him goes the player who carried the most iconic number in Albiceleste history for two decades. The question now is what happens to the shirt he leaves behind, and whether it can be put away for good.



According to Argentine outlet TyC Sports, Messi’s No.10 will not be used by any other player in the upcoming international break. The decision was made by head coach Lionel Scaloni, who is waiting to pick the “next” number 10 for Argentina.



The gesture is possible because the November matches are friendlies, where FIFA does not require squads to use consecutive numbers. That allows Scaloni to leave the shirt untouched for now, a symbolic tribute to the player who retired as the national team’s all-time leading scorer and most-capped player.



The answer for official competition, however, is different. FIFA rules require World Cup and Copa America squad lists to use consecutive numbers from 1 to 26, with a number assigned to every player on the roster. That means Argentina cannot leave the No.10 unused or retire it for official tournaments, no matter how symbolic the gesture would be.



Lionel Messi #10 of Argentina during the 2026 World Cup. (Getty Images)



The Diego Maradona precedent



This is not the first time Argentina has run into this wall. Ahead of the 2002 World Cup, the AFA tried to retire the No.10 as a tribute to Diego Maradona, whose career had already turned the shirt into much more than a number. The federation even proposed a squad numbered up to 24 that would skip the No.10, but FIFA rejected the request, citing the consecutive-numbering rule.


        


As a result, the shirt kept being worn by later generations of Argentine players, with Ariel Ortega wearing it in 2002, until it eventually reached Messi. With the same regulation still in place, any renewed push to retire it in his honor would face the same outcome.



Who could inherit the No.10?



The bigger question will arrive when Argentina returns to official competition: who takes the shirt next? Nico Paz is the name most often mentioned, as the Como 1907 playmaker operates in a similar position to Messi and wears the same number at his club. The doubt is whether a 22-year-old can handle the weight of that number so early in his international career.



His performances this season suggest he can. Paz has been one of the standouts of the 2026-27 campaign, with six goals and eight assists in 13 appearances across Serie A and the UEFA Champions League.



Nico Paz celebrates a goal for Como 1907. (Getty Images)



Still, Argentina has other options. Some believe the shirt might be better suited to a proven World Cup winner, with Alexis Mac Allister, Julian Alvarez and Enzo Fernandez floated as alternatives who already have the pedigree and experience to carry that responsibility. For now, Scaloni appears in no rush: by leaving the shirt without an owner, he buys time before making one of the most symbolic decisions of the new era.
